sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Explains Pesach Sheni through three introductions: the difference between the first and second months in divine service and in the Sefiros, and the concept of Pesach as a leap.

translations.translation: To understand the concept of Pesach Sheni,
and the Tzemach Tzedek explains in his maamar beginning with the words "Zeh"1,
that the concept of Pesach Sheni will be understood based on three introductions.
The first introduction is the difference between the first month
(Nissan)
and the second month
(Iyar)
in the service of man.
For in the month of Nissan,
whose focal point is the Exodus from Egypt,
it is the service of "turn away from evil,"
meaning that evil is in its full strength and the service is to turn away from evil,
to go out and flee from evil,
itkafya2.
And the service of the month of Iyar
[whose unique aspect, by which it is distinguished from the other months, is that on each of its days there is a specific mitzvah
(of Sefiras HaOmer)3]
is the service of Sefiras HaOmer,
whose concept is4
the refinement of the midos and their transformation to holiness,
it'hapcha.
And this is what is said5
"On the first of the second month... of their going out from the land of Egypt,"
that the first service of the Exodus,
the first month,
is itkafya of the sitra achara,
and afterwards comes the service of it'hapcha,
the second service of the Exodus,
the second month6.
And the second introduction is the distinction between these two months regarding the Sefiros.
For the first month is in Malchus,
the first Sefirah from below upward,
and the second month is in Yesod,
the second Sefirah7.
And it is explained in the maamar,
that these two introductions
[their concept of Nissan and Iyar in the service of man,
and their concept in the Sefiros]
are related to each other,
as explained in Torah Ohr, the maamar beginning "And behold we were binding sheaves"8
that the refinement through the tribes
(who were a chariot for the aspect of Malchus),
the first refinement,
is only the nullification of the yesh
(analogous to itkafya9),
and the refinement through Yosef HaTzaddik,
the aspect of Yesod,
the second refinement,
is that it be included in Elokus,
nullification in actual existence
(analogous to it'hapcha9).
And the third introduction is,
that the concept of Pesach,
Pesach from the term skipping and jumping10,
is a most lofty drawing down that cannot come through the order of hishtalshelus and only by way of a leap,
as explained in Likkutei Torah11.
And it is explained in the maamar,
that from this it is understood,
that also the concept of Pesach Sheni12
is a leap,
a drawing down that is above hishtalshelus.
And the difference between the first Pesach and Pesach Sheni is in the place and the concept in which this drawing down is drawn.
For by the first Pesach it is written13
"And Pesach to Hashem on the entrance,"
that the drawing down by way of a leap
(and Pesach)
was at the entrance,
the Sefirah of Malchus14,
and in the soul of man – in yirah tata'ah
("This is the gate to Hashem"15)
which is the root of "turn away from evil"16,
and the drawing down by way of a leap that is in Pesach Sheni is in the Sefirah of Yesod,
whose concept in the soul of man is connection and love17,
through which his midos are transformed to holiness,
it'hapcha.
